Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan will open the innings for Bangladesh. Nuwan Thushara will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Sri Lanka. Saif to face the first ball. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

171 has been the average first-innings winning score at this venue in T20s since the start of the year, and Sri Lanka are not far off that mark. This is Bangladesh's first game in Dubai, and it will be interesting to see how quickly their batters adapt to the conditions. It is all set up for an intriguing chase. Back in a bit for the second essay.

Sri Lanka were 98 for 4 with six overs to go, searching for some impetus in their innings. Up stepped Dasun Shanaka to provide that much-needed boost. With support at the other end limited, he remained undeterred as he took on the pacers once the spinners had completed their overs. Sri Lanka managed 70 runs off the final six overs, though two of those overs yielded just 11 runs in total, thanks to Mustafizur Rahman, whose efforts helped Bangladesh keep Sri Lanka under 170.

A six off the final ball of the innings, but not quite the finish Sri Lanka would have hoped for. Just 15 runs came off the last two overs, leaving them to settle for 168 on the board. It certainly is a competitive total, but whether it proves to be a match-winning one remains to be seen. After being asked to bat first, Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis gave Sri Lanka a brisk start. They managed to score 55 runs in the Powerplay despite Nissanka’s dismissal toward the end of it. Bangladesh struck back in the middle phase with a smart mix of spin and pace to apply the brakes on the scoring.

SIX! This time, Dasun Shanaka makes no mistake in reading the slower delivery! Taskin Ahmed bowls it on the shorter side, on off and middle. Shanaka opens his stance, winds up and pulls it with perfect timing. The ball sails over the deep square leg fence and he adds six more crucial runs on the board. Sri Lanka ends up putting 168 runs on the board!

OUT! CHARITH ASALANKA IS RUN OUT! Catch dropped but Tawhid Hridoy manages to recover and find the Sri Lankan skipper short of his crease. This is dug in short by Mustafizur and it is the off-pace delivery, outside off. Charith is made to reach out and he drags the pull in front of square on the leg side. Tawhid is a bit late in running off the ropes and puts in a dive. Tries to scoop the ball inches off the turf but fails to do so. The ball dribbles beside him off his hands. Hridoy is quick to get back up on his feet and fires in a throw on the bounce towards the batting end. The keeper, Litton Das is standing behind the stumps and he collects before breaking the stumps. Charith puts in a desperate dive and it is referred upstairs. The replays find Asalanka short of his crease despite the dive.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! It has been an arm-wrestle so far between the two teams. Sri Lanka raced away to a strong start with Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis getting off the blocks quickly, striking cleanly through the line. At that point, it looked like a true batting surface. However, as the innings progressed, the track has shown signs of being two-paced, making strokeplay a little harder. Bangladesh have pulled things back in fine fashion. From being 44/0, the island nation has slipped to 65/3 and is in need of some stability. Dasun Shanaka joins Kusal Perera out in the centre.

OUT! CASTLED! Smart bowling from Mahedi Hasan! Mahedi, while delivering, sees the batter set up for the reverse. He pulls the length back and follows the batter. Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back once again, on middle and leg. Kusal Mendis tucks it toward deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mahedi Hasan to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This is humongous from Kusal Mendis! Tossed up, fuller, on off. Kusal puts on his dancing shoes and he swings through to clear the long on fence for half a dozen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mahedi Hasan to Kusal Mendis, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Short, on off. Kusal Mendis eases it toward the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mahedi Hasan to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent running between the wickets! Mahedi Hasan bowls short, on middle, turns it toward the right-hander. Kusal Mendis hangs back and tucks it toward the vacant square leg region. The fielder charges from the deep mid-wicket region but is unable to stop the batters taking the second run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mahedi Hasan to Kusal Mendis, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Kamil Mishara is in at number 3. Mahedi Hasan comes into the attack, replacing Nasum Ahmed.

OUT! CAUGHT! Taskin Ahmed breaks through and he lets out a big roar! Angled into the right-hander, on a back of a length. Pathum looks to make use of the angle and pick it up off the pads as he did earlier in the over. The shot was on, given the short boundary behind square on the leg side. Nissanka gets it right off the toe end of the bat and skies it in front of deep mid-wicket. Saif Hassan runs across to his right in the deep and takes a safe catch at chest height. Pathum falls for 22 (15) and Sri Lanka are now 44/1 after 5 overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Saif Hassan b Taskin Ahmed
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Taskin Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Saif Hassan b Taskin Ahmed.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length, in the channel on off. Nissanka is a bit tentative to get on the front foot. Ends up chopping it down beside the wicket on the off side and wants to sneak in a quick single but Mendis says no. A wise decision from Kusal as Taskin was quick to get to the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Taskin Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On top of off, on a good length, Kusal covers the line and taps it in front of cover for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Taskin Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off by Taskin at 117.8 kph, on a back of a length, on the off stump. Pathum waits on the back foot and drops it with soft hands beside the strip on the leg side. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Taskin Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 135.2 kph, on a good length, on the off stump. Nissanka has a heave across the line and ekes out an inside edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Taskin Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Taskin Ahmed is greeted into the attack with a biggie! Slanting into the pads, on a length. Pathum just brings his wrists into play and plays the pick-up shot over the deep backward square leg fence for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Taskin Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker and on a nagging length, on off and middle, Mendis firms the drive down the deck where Ahmed is quick to move to his right and cut it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Proactive batting by Mendis! This is tossed up by Nasum, on a length, on off. Mendis skips down the track and even though he does not get entirely to the pitch of the ball, he goes through with the bat swing. Gets more than enough bat on it to clear the wide long off fence for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter and quicker, on off, Nissanka drops it with soft hands besides the pitch on the off side and is called through for a quick single by Mendis.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Nasum Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled in again into the right-hander, full in length, Pathum looks to drive it down the ground and plays slightly outside the line. Gets an inside edge onto the pads. Nearly sneaked through!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Nasum Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fired in by Nasum, full and on middle, blocked out by Nissanka.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nasum Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and on the off stump, Kusal cuts it late between short third and backward point. Shoriful Islam puts in a dive to his right at short third and gets a hand to it. Keeps the batters down to just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that a hat-trick of boundaries for Nissanka! Islam angles it across and the length is pulled back a bit. Pathum gets under the ball and swings through to go over the mid off fielder for another boundary. 15 runs off the over. Shoriful has gone for 23 in his first 2 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Two in two for Pathum Nissanka! Overcorrection from Shoriful as this is a half-volley, on the off pole. Pathum gets the front leg out of the way and drills it to the right of the diving mid off fielder for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Dispatched with disdain! Shoriful Islam bends his back and looks to go short, but fails to get it high enough. Shorfiul also errs in line and ends up offering width for Pathum to free his arms. Nissanka stands tall and pulls it well over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Angled away, on a short of a length, Kusal drops it beside him on the off side and takes a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, on top off, Pathum gets on his toes and taps it down in front of point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leading edge but safe! Shoriful Islam is not happy with the effort of the fielder charging in from the deep. Feels he should have done better there. Shoriful bowls it on a length, on middle. Kusal has a swipe across the line, but closes the bat face early. Gets a leading edge that goes up in the air but lands well in front of Shamim Hossain, charging in off the ropes at deep backward point. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled from a bit wide on the crease, attacking the front pad, on a length. Pathum defends it off the front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Nasum Ahmed to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spears in a full ball, on off, Mendis knocks it to long off and crosses over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done! Fractionally short and bowled with a flatter trajectory, around the off stump. Mendis rocks on the back foot and cuts it late. Manages to get it fine enough of the man at short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Darted in quicker and the length stays short, on off, Kusal dabs it down in front of cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower through the air and shorter as well, on off. Kusal presses back and the ball straightens a bit. Mendis stabs it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts with a flighted delivery from around the wicket, attacking the stumps. Kusal Mendis gets his bat out in front and blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Nasum Ahmed to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Early spin? Yep. Nasum Ahmed to operate from the other end.
Shoriful serves it on the fuller side, outside off. Pathum reaches out but the bat turns in his hand and he mistimes the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Going across the right-hander and the length is pulled back. Kusal pushes at the ball with hard hands. The outside edge is found and it trickles down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Kusal Mendis is up and running! A bit too full and a little too straight as well, on the pads. Mendis picks it up off the pads and deposits it over the deep square leg fence for the first six of the contest.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! This is pushed across the right-hander, on a length. Kusal plants his front foot forward and looks to swing through the line. Aims to go back over the bowler's head but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nearly sneaked through! Shoriful goes fuller in length and gets the ball to tail back in sharply. Mendis hurriedly gets his bat down and squeezes out an inside edge that dribbles to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pathum Nissanka and Sri Lanka are underway, albeit in a streaky fashion! Islam steams in from over the wicket and lands it on a good length. Shaping back into the right-hander, on middle. Nissanka does not move his feet much and pushes away from his body. Gets an inside edge that rolls wide of square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to get underway then. Litton Das and his men disperse from the huddle and take their respective positions on the field. It will be Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Returning to the side, left-arm quick, Shoriful Islam will get things going with the ball. Shoriful to Nissanka with a slip in place. Here we go!

We are moments away from the first ball in the Super Four stage, but before that, Charith Asalanka and Litton Das lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. Before that, a minute’s silence will be observed in memory of Mr. Suranga Wellalage, the father of Dunith Wellalage. The Sri Lankan players are also wearing black armbands as a mark of respect. It will be Bangladesh's national anthem first, followed by that of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Urooj Mumtaz is near the deck. She informs that this game will be played on pitch number 3, the same track where the UAE played against Pakistan. Adds that there is a 12-meter difference between the two square boundaries. Sanjay Manjrekar joins her and shares that this deck looks a bit drier. Manjrekar opines that Bangladesh's decision to bowl first is based on the past record of this venue. Sanjay further says that chasing will be easy if the dew comes in, but if it doesn't, batting second could be difficult given the dry nature of the surface.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Saif Hassan, Tanzid Hasan, Tawhid Hridoy, Litton Das (C/WK), Shamim Hossain, Jaker Ali, Mahedi Hasan (In for Nurul Hasan), Nasum Ahmed, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam (In for Rishad Hossain), Mustafizur Rahman.

Sri Lanka (Unchanged Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamil Mishara, Kusal Perera, Charith Asalanka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dunith Wellalage, Dushmantha Chameera, Nuwan Thushara.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, says that he would have bowled first as well, but he doesn't mind batting first as it's a used pitch. Continues that he is happy that new players are coming out from different regions of his country and he is happy that they are having a platform to perform. Ends up saying that they are going with the same playing XI.

The captain of Bangladesh, Litton Das admits that he is not sure how the wicket will play, but going by the numbers favouring the chasing side, they have made the decision to bowl first. Mentions that they, as a side, are excited to get the opportunity to play three games in the Super Four stage. Adds that he is happy with the way the team has performed so far. Informs that Nurul Hasan and Rishad Hossain are the ones to miss out with Mahedi Hasan and Shoriful Islam coming in for them.
TOSS - Litton Das calls it correctly, and Bangladesh have elected to BOWL first.

Dunith Wellalage has been spotted at the ground. Understandably, it’s a tough time for the 22-year-old, but it’s a commendable act to return and rejoin the squad. We wish him strength in these testing times.

Bangladesh clinched the T20I series in Sri Lanka’s backyard in July, but Sri Lanka won the group-stage meeting between the two sides quite convincingly, giving the island nation a slight edge. The Dubai pitches are no longer as conducive to hitting through the line as they once were, something evident even during the Champions Trophy earlier in the year. Similarly, the toss is not quite the be-all and end-all here, unlike the 2021 T20 World Cup in this part of the world, where winning the toss often meant winning the game. Stick around for the toss and team news.

Bangladesh managed wins over Hong Kong, China and Afghanistan but ultimately needed a favour from tonight’s opponents, as Sri Lanka’s victory over Afghanistan secured their qualification. Encouragingly, their top four have been among the runs, something that has troubled them in recent times. Tawhid Hridoy and Litton Das, in particular, will be central to their success. The gamble of going in with just four frontline bowlers and patching up the fifth bowler’s overs with part-timers backfired against Afghanistan. While it didn’t cost them the game, they did concede plenty of runs, and it leaves their team balance under the scanner.

Sri Lanka, the champions of the previous edition of the T20 Asia Cup, produced a flawless run in the group stage. Surprisingly, it was Hong Kong, China, that pushed them harder than either Bangladesh or Afghanistan. In the buildup, their heavy reliance on Pathum Nissanka was seen as a major concern, but that issue seems to have eased with Kusal Mendis, Kamil Mishara, and Kamindu Mendis all among the runs. The mood, though, turned sombre after the Afghanistan game with the sudden passing of Dunith Wellalage’s father. The update last night was that the left-arm spin bowling all-rounder was expected to rejoin the squad this morning and will be available for selection.

Hello, one and all! It’s time for the Super Four stage of the 2025 Asia Cup to kick off. From Group A, India and Pakistan have advanced, while Sri Lanka and Bangladesh made it through from Group B. The lineup is largely on expected lines, though some may have tipped Afghanistan to reach this stage given their impressive showing in the 2024 T20 World Cup. The Super Four will follow a single round-robin format, with the top two teams advancing to the final on 28th September. It all gets underway tonight with Sri Lanka taking on Bangladesh at the Dubai International Stadium.
... MATCH DAY ...

For the very first time in Asia Cup history, eight teams stepped up with fire in their eyes, all chasing the same dream. And now, the battle has narrowed down to just four contenders. From Group A, it is the heavyweights India and Pakistan, while Group B sends through Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, a group that proved to be far more intense from start to finish. The Super 4 stage kicks off with Sri Lanka taking on Bangladesh. Charith Asalanka's men topped their group, while Litton Das and his side secured the second spot. Both teams had to dig deep along the way. Sri Lanka, in all fairness, had a dominant run for ninety percent, but they were certainly pushed hard by Hong Kong, China, while Bangladesh had to survive a pressure-filled couple of do-or-die clashes, primarily one against Afghanistan. For Sri Lanka, the defending champions of the T20 Asia Cup, the real test begins now. They are one of only two sides still unbeaten, and overall, they will be satisfied with how they have lived up to expectations by keeping a spotless record with their star-studded squad. Pathum Nissanka sits on top of the run charts and is one of just three batters to cross the 100-run mark so far. His two vital half-centuries have once again underlined his role as the backbone of Sri Lanka’s top order. Adding to that, Kusal Mendis' return to form with a blazing 74 and Kamil Mishara's rise at number three have made the batting unit look even more formidable. The only area that needs ironing out is the middle order, which has shown signs of inconsistency and will face stiffer tests from here on. On the bowling front, Dushmantha Chameera and Nuwan Thushara have been reliable, with Chameera particularly standing out thanks to his game-changing four-wicket haul against Afghanistan. A major setback for Sri Lanka, though, is the absence of spin all-rounder Dunith Wellalage, who has flown back home after the sudden passing of his father. His availability for the coming games remains uncertain. The squad does have depth, with Kamindu Mendis contributing significantly so far and Janith Liyanage waiting in the wings, while the inclusion of Matheesha Pathirana is still under consideration. In spin, Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana remain the main threats, and their craft will be crucial once again on the slow, dry surfaces of the UAE. Bangladesh rolled the dice with four changes in their previous game, and it seems to have clicked. Their biggest worry had been an over-reliance on skipper Litton Das to carry the batting. The openers weren’t firing, the middle order wasn’t putting together stands, and partnerships in the middle overs were missing. While the middle-order issue still lingers, the new opening pair of Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan gave the side a solid start and took plenty of weight off Das’ shoulders. The tweak in the bowling unit also worked in their favor. Adding Nasum Ahmed as an extra spinner brought immediate dividends, with the left-armer proving a real handful. Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman continue to be steady performers with the ball, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib has provided sharp bursts of pace when needed. With this blend of balance and impact, Bangladesh will feel they are finally edging closer to the right formula as the competition heats up. When these two teams squared off in the league stage in Abu Dhabi, Sri Lanka came out on top with a fairly comfortable win. That result has only added fuel to Bangladesh’s fire, as they head into this clash determined to settle the score and turn the tables on the defending champions. In Dubai, these two have crossed paths only once, back in the 2022 Asia Cup, where Sri Lanka edged out a nail-biter. The overall head-to-head still tilts in favor of the Lankans 13-8, but recent history tells a different story. Since Bangladesh’s T20I series win on Sri Lankan soil just a couple of months ago, they actually hold the edge with three victories in the last five encounters. In Asia, the rivalry most spoken of is India vs Pakistan, but over the years, this 'serpentine' rivalry between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh has quietly produced far more competitive encounters than one-sided bummers. Another clash of the same vein is on the cards, one that promises intensity, commitment, and a fair bit of bite. A win here not only strengthens either side’s position but also hands them the momentum to ride on through the Super 4s.
